doc.title: Al Gafa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 2, 2023

title: Session with The Monkees and the value of permanent groups
summary: He did demo-turned-album work for The Monkees, found it just another job, and prefers permanent groups.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Okay. I’m looking on your list of recordings you’ve done with other people and it’s interesting that it goes from Carmen McRae to Paul Simon and then there’s an entry here about The Monkees.

Uh huh. Well you know that was in my studio days, probably somewhere between ’64 or ’68 or something like that, and The Monkees were a hot group and they were in recording and I got a call to go in and do this — it was a demo that stayed on the album. So that’s my recording scene with The Monkees. We did two or three tunes and — in a small studio, not a big studio, and they ended up on several of the albums.
Interesting. Not that much different from those early demos you did.
Right. Right. They were easy guys. Maybe they were easy because I don’t know if any of them had any talent except maybe David, the lead singer — I can’t remember his name.

Yeah. Yeah. Well I don’t know it could be, I don’t remember last names. And I think the drummer could play. The rest of them were nothing. And you know I don’t remember anything memorable. If you ask me what the name of the tune was or anything like that I wouldn’t know it. It was just another job you know.
Just another job. That’s a lot about what a music career is about, isn’t it?

Yeah you’re probably right there, yeah. I’ve been lucky. Because I’ve been lucky to be in more permanent situations than not. You know I’m in a lot of — and when you’re in a permanent situation you can really grow. Because it’s there, it’s going to be more of the same the next night and you can improve on what you got. Otherwise it’s — if you work a job here and you don’t see the same musicians for another two months it’s like a whole new ballgame as opposed to — that’s why I say I enjoy working with the same groups because I can write into the strengths, I can play into the strengths, and by doing both of those things you can raise the level of the group too.
